base_path.description: The projection's root directory, absolute and outside the colony root; the work tree of a workspace is `<base_path>/<ws>` (the directory `./mat` lays out). The owner sets it together with `sandbox.filesystem.write: [<the same path>, <git_dir>]` by `override_params` on this cell (the sandbox takes only literal paths). Empty: every op answers `no_base_path`.

git_dir.description: Where the repositories live: the repository of a workspace is the bare `<git_dir>/<ws>`. Absolute and outside `base_path` (not equal, not below, not above it), and granted in the sandbox of THIS cell alone -- `run` writes all of `base_path`, and a program it starts must never reach a repository's config, refs or attributes (GH #980). The directory exists before the cell spawns. Empty, relative or overlapping `base_path`: every op answers `no_git_dir`.

git_author.description: Author and committer of an export commit, `Name <mail>`; anything else falls back to the default.

remotes.description: Remote name -> URL or absolute path. A `remote`/`source` argument that is no name here is taken only as an absolute local path. A network remote also needs `sandbox.network: allow` by owner override -- this param never changes the sandbox. There is no credential path: a URL with a user or secret in it (`https://user@host`, `user@host:path`) is `credentials_unsupported` (OR-FJ-71); git runs without the host's environment, so no agent or helper supplies one either. A push target that is a local path (or `file://` URL) under, equal to or above `base_path` -- lexical or after symlinks -- is `remote_inside_base` before git runs: `run` writes all of `base_path`, and a local push runs the receiving repository's hooks in this cell's process. A local remote is granted to this cell in `sandbox.filesystem.write` like `git_dir`.

import_max_files.description: The most tree entries an import takes; a larger tree is `too_many_files` before anything is written.

import_max_bytes.description: The largest file an import writes (the file space's `write.max_bytes`); a larger one is skipped as `too_large`.

git_timeout_ms.description: Time cap of ONE git call; an overrun answers `git_timeout`. Stays below `external_timeout_ms`, the cap of the whole message.

description.purpose: git as the exchange format of a projection (K7): `ws_export_git` commits what `./mat` materialized -- only the manifest's paths, never a tool's artifacts beside them --, `ws_import_git` fetches a repository into the projection's own repository (a bare `<git_dir>/<ws>`, outside `base_path`, so no program of `run` reaches it) and writes the difference into the workspace through the file space, `ws_push` sends the exported head to a remote branch, `ws_pull` imports a remote branch. Since GH #980 `ws_export_git` and `ws_push` also take `args.root` instead of `hop.ws` (the root form a model's tool sends): the git projection of that root, a directory named `git.<segments>` under `base_path`; an export opens it as a workspace, exports and discards it, a push names only a remote of `remotes`; a refused open names the `view`. An export whose tree is the upstream's commits nothing and moves HEAD onto the upstream (a head beside it is kept as `refs/meclaw/superseded/<sha>` and named `previous`); an answer names the `subject` git logs for its commit, and every answer of the root form echoes its `root`. `git` runs as a subprocess with an argv list and an explicit environment (no host or user configuration, `core.autocrlf=false`), one time cap per call.
description.use_when: Inside a projection only, behind `in_proj` for the four git ops; answers of `./mat` and of the file space come back on `in_answer` under `op_id` `git:<job>.<n>`.
description.not_in_scope: git is never the store: nothing is read back out of `.git` into the hive except by an import. No force push and no rebase (a refused push is `push_rejected`, solved by a pull and a merge in the workspace); no `ws_commit` after an import (the caller commits); no `.gitignore` written; no credentials at all (a remote URL with userinfo is refused); nothing below a `.git` segment enters the hive or a commit, no `.git` in a work tree is ever read as a repository, and no hook or fsmonitor of a repository runs.
description.emits_meaning: `git_store` to `./store` between phases (`phase` names the job), `in_proj` `ws_materialize` to `./mat`, `in_ws` `ws_tree` (an import compares against it, an export learns the workspace root from it) and `in_write` `create`/`overwrite`/`remove` to the file space with `caller` 'projection', `answer` once per request.
description.consumes_meaning: A request on `in_proj`, answers on `in_answer`, the store's answers to its own bundles.
